subject.title: Feature Request: cron.defaults.delivery config for default delivery target

question: Should OpenClaw add a global `cron.defaults.delivery` primary delivery recipient default, and what exact safety and precedence rules should govern `announce`, `none`, `last`, account/thread routing, and `cron.failureDestination`?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix adds a new privacy-sensitive scheduled-output config surface and fallback policy that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Add Focused Delivery Default
options.body: Add `cron.defaults.delivery` with explicit job-level precedence, recipient validation, docs, CLI/UI support, and tests while keeping failure-notification defaults separate.

options.title: Improve Creation UX
options.body: Keep per-job delivery as the contract and reduce repetition through safer CLI/UI presets or route-preservation behavior instead of a new global recipient config.

options.title: Fold Into Output Routing
options.body: Defer the narrow default until the broader cron output-routing design decides channel, file, session, fallback, and status semantics.

recommendation.title: Add Focused Delivery Default
recommendation.body: Add `cron.defaults.delivery` with explicit job-level precedence, recipient validation, docs, CLI/UI support, and tests while keeping failure-notification defaults separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible routing signal from prior triage and adjacent config/security review context.
